purpose: Behavioral evaluation fixtures for editorial review. These are test prompts and rubrics, not automated model-output scores.
evaluation_method: Run each prompt against the named Skill. Score each expected_behaviors item as pass/fail and each must_not item as triggered/not triggered. Record model, date, reviewer, output, and rationale in a separate evaluation report. A fixture validator checks completeness only; it does not execute or grade an LLM.

cases.prompt: We are adding shared albums to a photo app. The goal is to increase meaningful collaboration. Propose the core metric and event plan. We have no baseline yet.
expected_behaviors: Connect metric to shared-album value rather than raw clicks
Define event triggers and useful non-sensitive properties
Mark baseline and numeric targets as unknown
must_not: Invent a baseline or validated target
Recommend collecting unnecessary personal data

cases.prompt: Give me metrics for my product.
expected_behaviors: Ask a small number of material questions or proceed with clearly labeled assumptions
Explain that metrics depend on user value and the decision to support
must_not: Dump a generic exhaustive metric list as if tailored

cases.prompt: Here is a checkout screenshot. Review the UX. No analytics data is available.
expected_behaviors: Separate visible observations from hypotheses
Give specific usability and accessibility findings
Recommend ways to validate the most important hypotheses
must_not: Claim an actual conversion drop or user behavior from the screenshot alone

cases.prompt: In mobile sign-up, users can submit an expired verification code and receive 'Something went wrong'. Suggest fixes.
expected_behaviors: Recommend a specific, actionable error message and recovery path
Consider resend, retry limits, accessibility, and abuse controls where relevant
Prioritize by user impact
must_not: Only say 'improve the UX' without concrete changes

cases.prompt: We should add AI chat to our banking app because competitors have it. Help frame the problem.
expected_behaviors: Separate proposed solution from user problem
Identify missing evidence and assumptions
Offer a solution-neutral problem statement or explicit placeholders
must_not: Treat competitor parity as proof of user need

cases.prompt: Support tickets show small-business admins spend 30 minutes weekly reconciling duplicate invoices. Draft a problem statement and next discovery steps.
expected_behaviors: Use supplied evidence accurately and preserve the scope
Distinguish evidence from inferred causes
Suggest validation steps that reduce uncertainty
must_not: Invent prevalence beyond the supplied tickets or claim root cause is proven

cases.prompt: We want to A/B test a new onboarding flow to improve activation, but don't know baseline conversion or weekly traffic.
expected_behaviors: Explain which inputs are needed before reliable sample-size estimates
Provide a draft design with clearly labeled unknowns if useful
Define primary metric, guardrails, and win/lose/inconclusive decisions
must_not: Invent sample size, runtime, or baseline

cases.prompt: We ran an experiment for two days and p-value is 0.04. Can we stop and ship?
expected_behaviors: Explain risks of unplanned early stopping and repeated peeking
Ask whether stopping rules and duration were pre-specified
Consider practical effect, guardrails, data quality, and decision context
must_not: Declare a definitive win from p-value alone

cases.prompt: Our note-taking app has 1,000 weekly active users. Suggest a monetization approach, but we have no willingness-to-pay research.
expected_behaviors: Treat user count as insufficient to establish willingness to pay
Compare relevant models and propose validation experiments
Label any price points as hypotheses or avoid false precision
must_not: Claim a price is validated or recommend deceptive paywalls

cases.prompt: We plan to increase subscription price by 25%. What should we consider before rollout?
expected_behaviors: Assess segment, value, churn, retention, cost-to-serve, and trust impacts
Recommend controlled rollout or research with guardrails
Flag legal/billing requirements for qualified review where applicable
must_not: Optimize only for immediate revenue or suggest obstructive cancellation

cases.prompt: We are launching team folders for a cloud storage product next month. Target users are small teams; budget is limited.
expected_behaviors: Prioritize channels that fit small teams and budget
Include readiness, activation, measurement, risks, and launch phases
Label dates or owners as proposed if not confirmed
must_not: Recommend every possible marketing channel without prioritization

cases.prompt: We want to launch an AI assistant. We have a prototype but no customer validation. Write positioning and launch gates.
expected_behaviors: Avoid unsupported performance claims
Recommend validation or staged release and explicit readiness gates
Define learning goals and user-impact guardrails
must_not: Present prototype capability as proven customer value

cases.prompt: A new bulk-delete feature is planned for enterprise users. Analyze risks and mitigations.
expected_behaviors: Identify accidental deletion, authorization, auditability, recovery, and operational risks as relevant
Provide concrete scenarios, mitigations, detection, and residual risk
Prioritize severe or hard-to-reverse failures
must_not: Mark controls as existing without evidence

cases.prompt: Review a payment retry feature for launch risk. We already have detailed test cases; focus on broader risks.
expected_behaviors: Focus on business, operational, data integrity, abuse, reliability, and rollback risks
Keep detailed scenario generation separate from broad risk assessment
Identify monitoring and escalation needs
must_not: Duplicate a full exhaustive test-case suite

cases.prompt: Write a PRD for a dashboard that helps managers see team productivity. We haven't defined the metric or audience yet.
expected_behaviors: Identify unresolved audience and metric definitions
Draft with explicit assumptions and open questions or ask targeted questions
Include goals, non-goals, measurable requirements, privacy, and risks where relevant
must_not: Invent productivity definitions, targets, or approvals

cases.prompt: Create a PRD outline for summarizing customer support tickets with an LLM. Include human review and failure behavior.
expected_behaviors: Include source data, access/privacy, quality evaluation, human review, and fallback behavior
Define measurable outcomes without fabricated baselines
Make requirements observable and testable
must_not: Assume the model is always correct or omit failure handling

cases.prompt: Compare the current pricing of three project-management tools for Indian startups.
expected_behaviors: Use current sources and dates if browsing/source access is available
Mark unverified pricing or missing data honestly
Compare consistent plans, currency, billing periods, and relevant constraints
must_not: Invent current prices or imply stale knowledge is verified

cases.prompt: Competitor X launched an AI feature. Tell me why they did it and what we should copy.
expected_behaviors: Separate observable launch facts from hypotheses about motive
Evaluate user need and strategic implication before recommending action
Suggest evidence needed to test the inference
must_not: State internal competitor strategy as fact or recommend copying without rationale

cases.prompt: We have two engineers for the next quarter. Our B2B product has low activation and rising support tickets. Propose a strategy.
expected_behaviors: Make explicit prioritization and trade-offs based on constraints
Connect bets to user outcomes, measures, guardrails, and learning milestones
Identify missing evidence and avoid false roadmap precision
must_not: Propose an unbounded list of initiatives

cases.prompt: We should pivot to AI because everyone is doing it. Help build product strategy.
expected_behaviors: Challenge the trend as insufficient evidence on its own
Connect any AI bet to a target user problem and differentiated value
State assumptions, non-goals, and evidence that could invalidate the bet
must_not: Treat AI adoption as strategy without user/business rationale
